pathway.title: Skeena Resources Ltd — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The credit is a completion credit, not a cash-flow credit, so leverage and coverage cannot rank it and the time to first production is the measure that matters. The statements show no revenue, derived EBITDA of negative CAD 121,007 thousand for the six months to June 30, 2026 and cash used in operations of CAD 30,235 thousand, against additions to mineral property, plant and equipment of CAD 203,600 thousand, which is 80.95% of cash spent on operations, construction, prepayments and leases. Until commissioning every coupon is paid from money raised, so each month of delay adds spending with no inflow. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C17

- Funding covers management's timetable only if spending slows as construction finishes, because the cushion beyond the first-production window is thin. Cash outside the interest reserve of CAD 505,433 thousand lasts 9.78 months at the second quarter 2026 spending pace of CAD 51,676.33 thousand a month and 12.06 months at the first-half pace of CAD 41,916.67 thousand a month, which ends between late April and early July 2027 against a management target of April to June 2027 for first production. Management states that the notes proceeds are sufficient to reach commercial production if the conditions precedent to the notes are met and the statements give no budget, so this is arithmetic on current pace and not a forecast, but it shows how little slack a delay would leave before more financing is needed. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 12; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8

- Liquidity is conditional rather than free, because most of the cash cannot be spent without a release. Restricted cash is 78.79% of total cash of CAD 635,661 thousand, unrestricted cash covers only 0.43 times the obligations of CAD 316,513 thousand due within a year, the statements name no committed facility after the US$350,000,000 term loan was terminated on April 10, 2026, and the statements say further financing is needed if the construction funds cannot be released or the notes prove insufficient. A failed release condition would turn a prefunded credit into a near-term liquidity problem, and the Gold Stream minimum unrestricted cash test of CAD 25,000 thousand, printed to March 31, 2026 and not restated, would be a further tripwire if it still applies. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4, 10–11, 14; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-05-15_ske-20260515xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; calculation C2; calculation C3

- Claims on the same production narrow what reaches noteholders after commissioning, and the ranking of part of them is not stated. The Gold Stream takes 3.52% of payable gold for the life of the mine at 10% of the market price, ranks pari passu with the notes and is carried at CAD 209,286 thousand; royalty liabilities of CAD 214,718 thousand include a 1% net smelter royalty and an option on more; together the claims outside Total Debt are CAD 424,004 thousand, or 40.15% of the notes' carrying value of CAD 1,055,969 thousand. If the stream completion test is not met by September 30, 2027 the stream percentage rises by 0.05 percentage points to 0.28 percentage points, which cuts the cash left for the coupon at about the time the interest reserve is used up. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 12, 14–15; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10

- Capital market access is demonstrated, which lowers refinancing and overrun-funding risk, but the evidence on its price is thin. The company placed US$750,000,000 of 8.50% notes due April 1, 2031, the notes' fair value of CAD 1,119,655 thousand is 6.03% above their carrying value, and common shares issued at CAD 14.70 in February 2025 were followed by options struck at CAD 36.32 on June 12, 2026, which indicates an equity value of about CAD 4,545,061 thousand, against which the notes' carrying value is 23.23%. An open equity market is the most plausible way to fund an overrun without adding senior claims, but the statements value the Gold Stream at a credit spread of 15.77% against an effective interest rate of 8.57% on the notes and print no price or yield, so the cost of new money is not established. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 12–13, 17; 6-K-EX-99.2_2025-11-13_ske-20251113xex99d2.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C19

- Currency and gold exposure is a reported-loss issue before production and the main commercial exposure after it. US dollar liabilities exceed US dollar assets by US$524,531,000 against a Canadian dollar functional currency with no hedging, a 1% move in the exchange rate changes the loss before tax by CAD 7,465 thousand, and the six months to June 30, 2026 already carried a foreign exchange loss of CAD 17,684 thousand, almost all of it unrealised. After commissioning, gold sold at a US dollar price will offset the US dollar coupon, but the gold price input fell 6.75% from USD 4,308 to USD 4,017 per ounce in six months and a 5% move in the forward gold curve moves the Gold Stream liability by CAD 10,464 thousand, so the exposure shifts from the balance sheet to the cash flow that services the notes. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 8, 10; calculation C15; calculation C16

- Governance is a secondary driver: there is no sponsor and no dividend, so the evidence points to dilution rather than cash leakage, and control is not established. Share-based payments were 49.96% of general and administration expenses in the first half of 2026 and outstanding awards equal 6.15% of shares outstanding; the audit committee has three independent members, management reports effective internal control at December 31, 2025 with KPMG LLP as auditor, but no holder list or board composition beyond the committee is supplied, which leaves sponsor and governance risk at Medium as Business & governance concludes. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 40-F_2025-12-31_ske-20251231x40f.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 17–18; calculation C22

runs.text: The first strength is prefunding: the notes placed CAD 683,168 thousand into restricted accounts, so construction and the first three coupons do not depend on market access in the next year, which lowers near-term default risk, although the release terms are unseen. The second is demonstrated capital market access, with US$750,000,000 of notes placed, equity raised in 2025 and a later share price indicator far above that issue price, which gives a route to fund an overrun and supports recovery through an equity cushion. The third is the project's status as fully permitted and under construction with a feasibility-level study base, which removes permitting from the near-term path and narrows the downside to execution and funding. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 8, 12, 17; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d1.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.2_2025-11-13_ske-20251113xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is the absence of revenue on a single project, which makes completion the only route to debt service and leaves leverage and coverage not calculable. The second is conditional liquidity, with 78.79% of cash restricted and no committed facility named. The third is the stack of claims on the same production, CAD 424,004 thousand outside Total Debt with the stream pari passu with the notes, which lowers cash for the coupon and recoveries. The fourth is an unhedged US dollar liability position and a gold price that moves the stream and royalty values and the future revenue of the project. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 10, 14–15; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The senior secured notes offering of US$750,000,000 completed on April 10, 2026 is the one new debt issue in the supplied filings. The notes bear 8.50% a year paid semi-annually, mature on April 1, 2031, are non-callable for two years and rank as senior secured obligations pari passu with the Gold Stream obligations and senior to subordinated debt. Proceeds of US$184,000,000 repurchased 66.67% of the Gold Stream, US$94,208,000 went to an interest reserve covering three semi-annual payments, US$400,000,000 went to a construction disbursement account and US$71,792,000 covered general and administrative expenses and issuance costs. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12–13

The offering replaced the undrawn US$350,000,000 Senior Secured Term Loan, which was terminated on April 10, 2026 with no draws made, and the buy-down followed an amending agreement of March 31, 2026 that also cancelled the option to draw an additional stream deposit. Change of control triggers an offer at 101% of principal, and the notes carry call prices of 104.25%, 102.125% and 100% in successive years from April 1, 2028. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-05-15_ske-20260515xex99d2.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14

In the first quarter of 2026 the company also granted third parties a 1% net smelter royalty and an option to elect a further 1.5% royalty, shares or a mix, in exchange for rights described only as certain rights for the duration of the project; the liabilities stand at CAD 78,709 thousand and CAD 136,009 thousand and an equity component of CAD 108,575 thousand was recorded. The cash received, if any, is not stated, and CAD 25,000 thousand of royalty obligations was prepaid in the second quarter. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 15; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-05-15_ske-20260515xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12

fields.value: The senior secured notes issued on April 10, 2026 are the only debt on Skeena's long-term debt lines, carried at CAD 1,055,969 thousand; with no revenue and negative EBITDA, repayment depends on construction funding and commissioning that management expects in 2027.

fields.value: Unrestricted cash at June 30, 2026 was CAD 134,808 thousand, with CAD 500,853 thousand more restricted to construction spending and interest on the notes; net debt on unrestricted cash is CAD 921,161 thousand. Six-month capital additions of CAD 203,600 thousand were met from cash on hand and note proceeds, while operations used CAD 30,235 thousand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The balance sheets print no debt line at December 31, 2024, September 30, 2025 or March 31, 2026 and a dash at December 31, 2025, so funded debt first appears with the US$750,000,000 senior secured notes issued on April 10, 2026, carried at CAD 1,055,969 thousand on June 30, 2026 against CAD 1,036,761 thousand of principal translated at issuance. The statements show no revenue and the derived EBITDA is negative in every period, CAD 22,065 thousand negative in the second quarter of 2026, so debt over EBITDA is not a usable measure and creditors rely on construction funding and, after commissioning, mine cash flow to carry the 8.50% coupon. The consequence is that leverage cannot rank this credit and the liquidity and funding analysis has to carry the judgement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest paid is not stated in any period, and the first interest payments on the notes are covered by an interest reserve of CAD 130,228 thousand deposited on April 10, 2026 for three semi-annual payments, so early coupons do not draw on operating cash. Interest and finance fee expense of CAD 19,851 thousand for the six months to June 30, 2026 is only the part not capitalised, because CAD 18,730 thousand of borrowing cost net of interest income went into mineral property and construction in progress. Interest cover is therefore not stated, and the reserve moves the first real coupon test to about eighteen months after issue, which on management's timetable is after the first production.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating activities used CAD 30,235 thousand in the six months to June 30, 2026 against CAD 38,699 thousand a year earlier, so the cash cost of running the company is small beside construction: additions to mineral property, plant and equipment were CAD 203,600 thousand against CAD 93,412 thousand a year earlier, with a further CAD 9,144 thousand of construction prepayments. Working capital moved little except accounts payable, which absorbed CAD 6,675 thousand. Capital spend, not operations, sets the funding need, and it was met from note proceeds and from CAD 199,176 thousand of restricted cash released, so release of the remaining restricted funds is the dependency that matters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Unrestricted cash was CAD 134,808 thousand at June 30, 2026 against undiscounted obligations due within one year of CAD 316,513 thousand, which include CAD 138,109 thousand of contractual commitments and CAD 88,581 thousand of long-term debt payments; restricted cash of CAD 500,853 thousand sits in the construction disbursement account and the interest reserve. The statements say further financing is needed if the construction funds cannot be released or the notes prove insufficient, and the statements name no committed facility or letter of credit after the term loan was terminated. Liquidity therefore turns on the release mechanics of restricted funds, and a creditor should read the CAD 635,661 thousand of total cash as conditional rather than free.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Skeena Resources Ltd (ske), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, operating model, transactions, ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour that matter to a creditor, drawn from the supplied filings. No sponsor, ratings, quotes, peers or executed legal documents are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Skeena is a single-project gold and silver developer whose creditors depend on completing Eskay Creek, where management targets first production in the second quarter of 2027, so execution and funding release, not governance, drive creditor outcomes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company has no revenue and discloses no sponsor or controlling holder, while the April 2026 financing placed CAD 683,168 thousand of note proceeds in restricted accounts and a gold stream and royalty liabilities already claim part of future production. Creditor cash-flow protection therefore begins only after commissioning, and the evidence on control and legal capacity is absent rather than reassuring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Construction and commissioning risk on one project dominates the credit. Eskay Creek is described as fully permitted and under construction, management expects initial production and cash flow in the second quarter of 2027 and commercial production in 2027, and until then there is no revenue. The August 2026 risk language names construction delays, cost overruns, commissioning or ramp-up failure and inability to access restricted funds, so a slip extends the period over which the notes are serviced from restricted funds and cash on hand, and creditors are underwriting a timetable rather than current earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 financing protects construction but makes the release of restricted funds a condition of credit support. The US$750,000,000 senior secured notes issued on April 10, 2026 carry an interest reserve of US$94,208,000 for three semi-annual payments and a construction disbursement account of US$400,000,000, and the statements say further financing is needed if the funds cannot be released or the notes prove insufficient. A delay in release would force a raise during construction, which weakens the creditors' position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Part of future production is already sold or burdened, which narrows the cash flow available to creditors. After the April 2026 buy-down the gold stream delivers 3.52% of payable gold for the life of the mine at 10% of the market price, and a 1% net smelter royalty and an option on a further royalty or shares were granted in 2026, while the March 2026 statements describe the project as subject to royalties of 4% to 5.5% without saying whether that range includes the new grants. These claims reduce revenue per ounce before the notes are paid, and the ranking of the royalty liabilities is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance disclosure is adequate for monitoring but silent on who controls the company. The audit committee has three independent members, KPMG LLP audits the annual statements and internal control over financial reporting was effective at December 31, 2025, but no holder list, sponsor or board composition beyond the committee is supplied, and the share count rose by 3.16% between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026. With no sponsor there is no sponsor support or extraction evidence either way, so control risk is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No distribution, acquisition or amendment history appears, so there is no evidence of extraction, but the history is short. The cash flow statements show no dividend line in any period supplied, and the only creditor-relevant actions in the statements are the 2026 financing, the stream buy-down, the royalty grants and a prepayment of royalty obligations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management pay is largely share-based and tied to milestones the statements do not define. Share-based payments were CAD 21,690 thousand of CAD 43,418 thousand of general and administration expenses in the first half of 2026, or 49.96%, and a grant of performance share units to officers on February 9, 2026 vests on a company milestone. Outstanding awards equal 6.15% of shares outstanding; the cost is non-cash but adds dilution, and whether the milestones include construction completion is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 17–18; calculation C2; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the view that execution and funding release dominate is the way the 2026 financing is built: the construction disbursement account was funded at issue, the interest reserve covers the first three coupons, the project is described as fully permitted, and the buy-down cut the gold stream to 3.52% of payable gold. The valuation inputs in the statements also use a gold price of USD 4,017 per ounce at June 30, 2026, which, if it holds, favours the project economics, although costs are not supplied. These facts make a funding failure before commissioning less likely than the risk language alone suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would soften if restricted funds were released on schedule, ore mining and stockpiling began on the timetable management gives, the stream completion test were met before September 30, 2027 and the updated technical report confirmed the production profile and mine life. It would harden on a delay in grid energization or commissioning, a cost overrun that exhausts the construction account, a successful permit challenge or evidence that the restricted funds cannot be released when required.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual information form, management's discussion and any construction budget are not supplied, so the schedule, cost to complete and reserve base behind the second-quarter 2027 target are not established, and the finding that construction risk dominates rests on management's own timetable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No holder list, board composition beyond the audit committee or sponsor information is supplied, so the absence of a controlling holder or sponsor is an absence of disclosure and the governance finding cannot rule out concentrated control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The notes indenture and the stream and royalty agreements are not supplied, so ranking, guarantees, security and covenants rest on summaries in the statement notes, and the finding that part of future production is burdened cannot be sized beyond the percentages printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest statements are for June 30, 2026, so whether restricted funds have been released since is not established, and the funding-release finding describes the position at that date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The senior secured notes offering of US$750,000,000 completed on April 10, 2026 is the one new debt issue in the supplied filings. The notes bear 8.50% a year paid semi-annually, mature on April 1, 2031, are non-callable for two years and rank as senior secured obligations pari passu with the Gold Stream obligations and senior to subordinated debt. Proceeds of US$184,000,000 repurchased 66.67% of the Gold Stream, US$94,208,000 went to an interest reserve covering three semi-annual payments, US$400,000,000 went to a construction disbursement account and US$71,792,000 covered general and administrative expenses and issuance costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The offering replaced the undrawn US$350,000,000 Senior Secured Term Loan, which was terminated on April 10, 2026 with no draws made, and the buy-down followed an amending agreement of March 31, 2026 that also cancelled the option to draw an additional stream deposit. Change of control triggers an offer at 101% of principal, and the notes carry call prices of 104.25%, 102.125% and 100% in successive years from April 1, 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the first quarter of 2026 the company also granted third parties a 1% net smelter royalty and an option to elect a further 1.5% royalty, shares or a mix, in exchange for rights described only as certain rights for the duration of the project; the liabilities stand at CAD 78,709 thousand and CAD 136,009 thousand and an equity component of CAD 108,575 thousand was recorded. The cash received, if any, is not stated, and CAD 25,000 thousand of royalty obligations was prepaid in the second quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Skeena presents medium sponsor and governance risk on mixed and incomplete evidence. The key supported behaviour is a financing built with locked accounts and an interest reserve, which matters because it protects construction and early coupons while making release a condition, and it implies liquidity that is conditional rather than free. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any distribution, sponsor or amendment history. Further analysis requires the holder list, the indenture and the stream and royalty agreements. Governance review completed with limitations; sponsor and governance risk level: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Skeena Resources Ltd (ske), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated fundamental credit view of the issuer, built from the supplied filings and the earlier work on source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance. No ratings, quotes, peers or executed legal documents are supplied, and no rating or security recommendation is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Skeena is a pre-revenue, single-project developer whose senior secured notes rest on construction funding and on Eskay Creek reaching production on management's 2027 timetable, so creditors are underwriting completion risk that prefunding mitigates but does not remove. The profile is weak on today's fundamentals: there is no revenue, derived EBITDA is negative in every period, and leverage cannot rank the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Prefunding is the main support: cash of CAD 134,808 thousand and restricted cash of CAD 500,853 thousand at June 30, 2026 exceed obligations due within a year of CAD 316,513 thousand, and a reserve funds the first three coupons. These balances already include the April 10, 2026 notes issuance; a pro forma position for earlier dates is not established. The main downside is a delay or overrun that outlasts the funds before first cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4, 10–12; calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit is a completion credit, not a cash-flow credit, so leverage and coverage cannot rank it and the time to first production is the measure that matters. The statements show no revenue, derived EBITDA of negative CAD 121,007 thousand for the six months to June 30, 2026 and cash used in operations of CAD 30,235 thousand, against additions to mineral property, plant and equipment of CAD 203,600 thousand, which is 80.95% of cash spent on operations, construction, prepayments and leases. Until commissioning every coupon is paid from money raised, so each month of delay adds spending with no inflow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Funding covers management's timetable only if spending slows as construction finishes, because the cushion beyond the first-production window is thin. Cash outside the interest reserve of CAD 505,433 thousand lasts 9.78 months at the second quarter 2026 spending pace of CAD 51,676.33 thousand a month and 12.06 months at the first-half pace of CAD 41,916.67 thousand a month, which ends between late April and early July 2027 against a management target of April to June 2027 for first production. Management states that the notes proceeds are sufficient to reach commercial production if the conditions precedent to the notes are met and the statements give no budget, so this is arithmetic on current pace and not a forecast, but it shows how little slack a delay would leave before more financing is needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 12; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is conditional rather than free, because most of the cash cannot be spent without a release. Restricted cash is 78.79% of total cash of CAD 635,661 thousand, unrestricted cash covers only 0.43 times the obligations of CAD 316,513 thousand due within a year, the statements name no committed facility after the US$350,000,000 term loan was terminated on April 10, 2026, and the statements say further financing is needed if the construction funds cannot be released or the notes prove insufficient. A failed release condition would turn a prefunded credit into a near-term liquidity problem, and the Gold Stream minimum unrestricted cash test of CAD 25,000 thousand, printed to March 31, 2026 and not restated, would be a further tripwire if it still applies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4, 10–11, 14; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-05-15_ske-20260515xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Claims on the same production narrow what reaches noteholders after commissioning, and the ranking of part of them is not stated. The Gold Stream takes 3.52% of payable gold for the life of the mine at 10% of the market price, ranks pari passu with the notes and is carried at CAD 209,286 thousand; royalty liabilities of CAD 214,718 thousand include a 1% net smelter royalty and an option on more; together the claims outside Total Debt are CAD 424,004 thousand, or 40.15% of the notes' carrying value of CAD 1,055,969 thousand. If the stream completion test is not met by September 30, 2027 the stream percentage rises by 0.05 percentage points to 0.28 percentage points, which cuts the cash left for the coupon at about the time the interest reserve is used up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 12, 14–15; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital market access is demonstrated, which lowers refinancing and overrun-funding risk, but the evidence on its price is thin. The company placed US$750,000,000 of 8.50% notes due April 1, 2031, the notes' fair value of CAD 1,119,655 thousand is 6.03% above their carrying value, and common shares issued at CAD 14.70 in February 2025 were followed by options struck at CAD 36.32 on June 12, 2026, which indicates an equity value of about CAD 4,545,061 thousand, against which the notes' carrying value is 23.23%. An open equity market is the most plausible way to fund an overrun without adding senior claims, but the statements value the Gold Stream at a credit spread of 15.77% against an effective interest rate of 8.57% on the notes and print no price or yield, so the cost of new money is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 12–13, 17; 6-K-EX-99.2_2025-11-13_ske-20251113xex99d2.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Currency and gold exposure is a reported-loss issue before production and the main commercial exposure after it. US dollar liabilities exceed US dollar assets by US$524,531,000 against a Canadian dollar functional currency with no hedging, a 1% move in the exchange rate changes the loss before tax by CAD 7,465 thousand, and the six months to June 30, 2026 already carried a foreign exchange loss of CAD 17,684 thousand, almost all of it unrealised. After commissioning, gold sold at a US dollar price will offset the US dollar coupon, but the gold price input fell 6.75% from USD 4,308 to USD 4,017 per ounce in six months and a 5% move in the forward gold curve moves the Gold Stream liability by CAD 10,464 thousand, so the exposure shifts from the balance sheet to the cash flow that services the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 8, 10; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance is a secondary driver: there is no sponsor and no dividend, so the evidence points to dilution rather than cash leakage, and control is not established. Share-based payments were 49.96% of general and administration expenses in the first half of 2026 and outstanding awards equal 6.15% of shares outstanding; the audit committee has three independent members, management reports effective internal control at December 31, 2025 with KPMG LLP as auditor, but no holder list or board composition beyond the committee is supplied, which leaves sponsor and governance risk at Medium as Business & governance concludes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 40-F_2025-12-31_ske-20251231x40f.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 17–18; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak reading is that the financing was sized for construction: total cash is 2.01 times the obligations due within a year, a reserve funds the first three coupons, the project is described as fully permitted, feasibility studies from 2021 to 2023 are referred to in the statements and the annual report lists consents from eight independent engineering and environmental firms. The equity value indicated by option pricing is far above the notes' carrying value, the notes carry a fair value above carrying value, and a gold price near the USD 4,017 per ounce used in the valuations would favour project economics if costs are as management describes. If construction stays on schedule these facts make a funding failure before commissioning less likely than the absence of revenue suggests; what they cannot show is operating cost, which decides whether mine cash flow covers the coupon.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4, 8, 12, 17; 6-K-EX-99.2_2025-11-13_ske-20251113xex99d2.htm.jsonl, page 16; 40-F_2025-12-31_ske-20251231x40f.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C3; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Evidence that would soften the view is release of restricted funds on schedule, ore mining and stockpiling starting on the timetable, spending in the third quarter of 2026 and later running below the first-half pace, initial production reported in the second quarter of 2027 and the stream completion test met before September 30, 2027, which keeps the stream at 3.52% of payable gold. Evidence that would harden it is spending near the second-quarter pace without matching progress, any change in the release conditions, new financing that ranks with or ahead of the notes, a fall in the notes' fair value below carrying value, or disclosure of a cost per ounce above what management implies by calling the mine one of the lowest-cost open-pit mines.

fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 8, 14; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.value: - No mine plan, throughput, grade, recovery, operating cost per ounce or sustaining capital is in the supplied files, so cash flow after commissioning cannot be sized and the conclusion that mine cash flow can carry the 8.50% coupon is a judgement about structure, not a calculation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The months of funding use average spending in the first half and second quarter of 2026 and the interest reserve as deposited on April 10, 2026, because no budget and no reserve balance at June 30, 2026 are printed, so the conclusion that the cushion beyond the first-production window is thin moves with the pace assumed.

fields.value: - No peer, sector or price series is supplied beyond the issuer's two gold price inputs, so the judgement that the business profile sits below that of producing gold issuers, and the reading of sector direction, rest on structure and not on benchmark data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The statements value the Gold Stream at a company credit spread of 15.77% while the notes carry an effective interest rate of 8.57%, and they print no price, yield or spread for the notes, so the cost of any additional financing, and with it how easily an overrun could be funded, is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Skeena Resources Limited is a British Columbia development-stage mining company whose credit is one asset, the Eskay Creek Gold-Silver Project in the Golden Triangle, which management describes as fully permitted and under construction. The statements show no revenue and no segment schedule, so the business model is a construction project that will sell gold and silver once commissioned, and cash flow visibility is nil until then. Management expects initial production and cash flow in the second quarter of 2027 and commercial production in 2027, and a gold stream and royalties already claim part of future production, so debt service capacity, liquidity preservation and refinancing confidence all depend on completion on that timetable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4, 14–15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-24_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 1; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management calls the mine one of the world's highest-grade and lowest-cost open-pit precious metals mines with silver by-product output, but no grade, cost or output figure is supplied to test the claim. The statements refer to a 2021 prefeasibility study, a 2022 feasibility study and a 2023 updated feasibility study, and the August 2026 release says an updated technical report is planned that could change the production profile and mine life, so the production base behind the timetable is subject to revision.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No parent, sponsor or controlling holder is named and the statements are consolidated for Skeena Resources Limited with no subsidiary, guarantor or co-issuer identified, so structural subordination of the notes to subsidiary creditors is not established. The notes rank pari passu with the Gold Stream obligations, which carry general security and a share pledge in favour of the stream holder as printed to March 2026, and the notes' own collateral is not stated, so the position of noteholders against the stream holder on the same assets is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy shows no dividend in any period supplied and equity raised in 2025, and the share count rose by 3.16% between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 through option exercises and vesting of share units. Business & governance puts sponsor and governance risk at Medium on incomplete evidence: the evidence shows no extraction and the filings supply no holder list, so creditor alignment is plausible but unproven.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.2_2025-11-13_ske-20251113xex99d2.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no revenue to test for durability. After commissioning revenue will come from gold and silver sold as concentrate, less the stream and royalty deductions, and its predictability will turn on throughput, metal prices and smelter terms, none of which the filings let a reader test. The May 2026 release lists concentrate sales risks, including smelter terms that are market dependent, possible export restrictions on critical minerals that limit the choice of smelters, and geopolitical risk in contracting with customers in regions such as China, so revenue visibility after commissioning rests on contracts the filings do not describe and a policy change could cut the buyers available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost cannot be assessed beyond the construction stage. Cash used in operations was CAD 30,235 thousand in the first half of 2026 against additions of CAD 203,600 thousand, and general and administration expenses of CAD 43,418 thousand included share-based payments of CAD 21,690 thousand. Once built, an open-pit mine is mostly fixed cost, so margins will be sensitive to throughput and recoveries, while the stream, delivered at 10% of the market price, and the royalties scale with revenue and so thin the cash left for debt without adding fixed cost. Cost flexibility before commissioning is low because construction is committed: contractual commitments due within a year are CAD 138,109 thousand, and although some may contain cancellation clauses the statements say they are disclosed on management's intent to fulfil them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity dominates at this stage. Additions to mineral property, plant and equipment are 80.95% of first-half cash spending, and the statements do not split maintenance from growth capital, so capex flexibility over the debt life cannot be assessed. Conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow is not calculable because EBITDA is negative; the only free cash flow evidence is outflow, with CAD 242,979 thousand used on operations, additions and prepayments in the six months to June 30, 2026, so creditors depend on completion rather than on conversion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C6; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry works through the cost curve because a gold producer takes the gold price, and Eskay Creek's cost position is asserted by management and not evidenced, so margin resilience in a gold price fall is not established. Barriers to new entrants are permits and capital, and the project already holds its permits, but the release risk language names changes to, delays in or challenges to permits and the environmental assessment certificate, so permit durability stays a creditor risk. Substitutes are not a driver for gold, and silver adds a second price exposure. Concentrate buyers and smelters set terms and the May 2026 release names smelter terms and export restrictions as risks. Contractors, equipment, power and labour matter during construction, and the August 2026 release names cost inflation, tariffs, supply-chain disruption, grid energization and contractor performance, each of which raises the chance of an overrun that would be paid from a finite fund.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four groups of external factors matter to the credit. Regulatory and Indigenous relationships and permits are named risks, and the 2024 court decision on rights to stored materials at Albino Lake was sent back for rehearing with no outcome printed in the 2026 statements, although the company says it should not affect the carrying value of Eskay. The gold price, exchange rate and interest rates are unhedged, and the statements name inflation among cost risks. Metallurgical testwork and the updated technical report can still change the production profile and mine life.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are prefunded construction with a reserve for the first three coupons, a fully permitted project and open debt and equity markets. The weaknesses are no revenue, one asset, restricted liquidity, claims from the stream and royalties on the same production, and an unhedged US dollar liability position. Opportunities are an updated technical report that improves the production profile, completion before September 30, 2027 that keeps the stream at 3.52% of payable gold, and redemption at fixed prices from April 1, 2028 that allows refinancing once cash is generated. Threats are construction delay or overrun, failure to release restricted funds, a lower gold price and a permit or title challenge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4, 12–14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; calculation C3; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is prefunding: the notes placed CAD 683,168 thousand into restricted accounts, so construction and the first three coupons do not depend on market access in the next year, which lowers near-term default risk, although the release terms are unseen. The second is demonstrated capital market access, with US$750,000,000 of notes placed, equity raised in 2025 and a later share price indicator far above that issue price, which gives a route to fund an overrun and supports recovery through an equity cushion. The third is the project's status as fully permitted and under construction with a feasibility-level study base, which removes permitting from the near-term path and narrows the downside to execution and funding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 8, 12, 17; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d1.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.2_2025-11-13_ske-20251113xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is the absence of revenue on a single project, which makes completion the only route to debt service and leaves leverage and coverage not calculable. The second is conditional liquidity, with 78.79% of cash restricted and no committed facility named. The third is the stack of claims on the same production, CAD 424,004 thousand outside Total Debt with the stream pari passu with the notes, which lowers cash for the coupon and recoveries. The fourth is an unhedged US dollar liability position and a gold price that moves the stream and royalty values and the future revenue of the project.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 10, 14–15; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is weak today and cannot yet be measured in the usual way. Scale and diversification are weak because the issuer has no revenue and one project in one jurisdiction, and the competitive advantage claimed by management is not evidenced. Cost and capex flexibility are low because construction is committed, margin stability cannot be assessed without revenue, and free cash flow is an outflow. Capital market access is demonstrated, since a large secured issue and an equity raise have been completed, but it is priced at an 8.50% coupon with a covenant package the filings do not show. Liquidity covers the stated timetable on management's own assertion but falls short on the current spending pace, and it is conditional on release of restricted funds; financial policy is neutral so far, with no distributions and dilution through share-based pay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3, 10–11, 17–18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trend is dominated by the April 10, 2026 financing. Funded debt first appears with the notes, carried at CAD 1,055,969 thousand, and net debt on unrestricted cash is CAD 921,161 thousand at June 30, 2026, which already includes the April 10, 2026 notes issuance; a pro forma net debt for the earlier balance sheet dates is not established. The Gold Stream liability fell from CAD 421,902 thousand at December 31, 2025 to CAD 209,286 thousand after a buy-down that cost US$184,000,000, which swaps a revenue-linked claim whose buy-down price embedded an imputed 18% return for notes at an 8.50% coupon, adding US$15,640,000 a year of fixed interest on that portion before production but leaving more of the future gold revenue to the company. Key missing datapoints are full-year statements, cash interest paid, operating cost and the indenture covenants.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 12–14; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-05-15_ske-20260515xex99d2.htm.jsonl, page 10; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 months to 24 months the outcome turns on construction and commissioning. Tailwinds are a permitted project, funded construction, a gold price near USD 4,017 per ounce in the valuation inputs and an equity market that has accepted the company's shares. Headwinds are execution risk on a single project, spending at a pace that leaves little slack beyond the first-production window, and a calendar that crowds together the stream completion test on September 30, 2027, the end of the reserve cover around eighteen months after issue and the first date of fixed redemption prices, April 1, 2028. The fourth semi-annual coupon, about two years after issue, is the first that must be paid from operating cash or other funds, so first production needs to arrive well before it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 8, 12–14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the notes are the only debt maturity, due in full on April 1, 2031, with redemption prices starting at 104.25% from April 1, 2028 and falling to par from 2030, and a right to redeem up to 40% with equity proceeds at 108.5% before April 1, 2028. A producing mine would allow refinancing or equity-funded paydown on those terms, while a delayed one would leave the single maturity to be met from a smaller cash cushion. Sector headwinds are cost inflation, tariffs and smelter and export policy, and the sector tailwind is the gold price level, which also raises the stream and royalty claims in value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a construction or commissioning delay on the single project. Management's own risk list names delays in grid energization, commissioning or ramp-up and cost overruns, so the scenario starts with a delay of a quarter or more to initial production. The first operational break is that ore mining and stockpiling slip, so the mill is not fed on time and no concentrate is sold. The financial transmission is that spending continues at CAD 41,916.67 thousand to CAD 51,676.33 thousand a month with no inflow, so cash outside the interest reserve of CAD 505,433 thousand is used up between late April and early July 2027, and the statements say additional financing would then be needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The consequences follow in order. If the completion test is not met by September 30, 2027 the stream percentage steps up, by 0.05 percentage points if completion falls in the first quarter after that date and by 0.28 percentage points if it falls after the third, and the fourth coupon, about two years after issue, may fall due before operating cash arrives. New money would be raised during construction, probably as equity given the indicated equity cushion, or as debt or a stream whose cost the statements do not establish, since the stream is valued at a 15.77% credit spread. Management's levers are limited: committed spending is CAD 138,109 thousand within a year, marketable securities are CAD 14,240 thousand and equity is the main source. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress if first production arrives in the second quarter of 2027 and spending slows as construction ends, and insufficient for a delay beyond about a quarter without new money, so default risk before commissioning is driven by funding access rather than by operations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-08-13_ske-20260813xex99d2.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 8, 10–11, 14; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Skeena presents a weak business profile for a leveraged credit today, with no revenue and one project, supported by prefunded construction, a permitted project and open capital markets. Against typical leveraged gold issuers, which earn operating cash flow, its profile is weaker by construction, although no peer figures are supplied. Cash-flow durability cannot yet be established because there is no operating history to measure and no cost data to size margins. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on commissioning on schedule, the gold price and the cost of any new money. The primary downside path is a construction delay that outlasts restricted funds before first cash flow. Further analysis would require operating cost and production data, the construction budget, the indenture and stream agreement and statements after June 30, 2026.
